text:
A young tiger named Raja lived deep in the jungle, where he spent his days hunting and roaming. One evening, he smelled something incredible drifting from a village nearby—spices, rice, and something he couldn't name. Curious, he crept closer and saw a grandmother stirring a huge pot of biryani. The aroma made him forget all about hunting.

The next day, Raja returned and watched from the shadows as she cooked. He memorised every step: the ginger-garlic paste, the fried onions, the layers of rice and meat, the dum on low heat. When she left, he tried it himself with whatever he could find—wild herbs, a stolen pot, some rice from a broken sack. His first attempt was a disaster, burnt and tasteless, but he didn't give up.

Weeks passed, and Raja kept practising. Slowly, his biryani improved. One day, the grandmother returned to find a perfectly cooked pot waiting for her, still warm, with a single tiger pawprint in the sand beside it. She smiled, took a bite, and whispered, "Not bad, Raja. Not bad at all." From that day on, the jungle had the only tiger in the world who could make biryani as good as any grandmother's. 🐅🍛
